# BPCS Interlock Specification Template

**Rule that prevents duplicated setpoints:** every number (setpoint, delay, deadband) lives in one place, the **Parameter Register** (a single spreadsheet or database, one row per parameter, each with a unique ID). The interlock sheet, the configuration, and the FAT script all cite the parameter ID. The sheet may display the current value for readability, but it is marked "from register" and is never edited here.

---

## Part A: Template

### 1. Identification
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID | `<UNIT>-IL-<nnn>` |
| Title | |
| Unit / Area | |
| Revision / Date / Author / Approver | |
| Legacy source reference | Printout / C&E drawing no., sheet, rung or block |
| New DCS controller / module / function block | |

### 2. Classification and Purpose
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Layer | BPCS (confirm not credited in the SRS or LOPA as an IPL with a SIL claim) |
| Hazard / Process intent | What it protects against |
| Consequence if it fails to act | |
| Credit taken in PHA/LOPA? | Y/N and reference. If Y, stop and review whether it belongs in the SIS. |

### 3. Inputs
| Tag | Description | Signal type / range | Quality-bad action | Source (I/O address or soft tag) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### 4. Trip Logic
- Plain-language statement: "IF ... THEN ..."
- Logic expression using tags and parameter IDs only, e.g. `PT-xxxx.PV < [P-ID]` for `[P-ID2]` seconds
- Voting (1oo1, 2oo3, etc.) and handling of a failed or bad-quality input

### 5. Parameters (references only)
| Param ID | Meaning | Value (from register) | Unit | Register location |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Include setpoint, reset/deadband, on-delay, off-delay, and alarm pre-trip.

### 6. Permissives, Bypasses, Overrides
| Item | Tag | Condition | Authority / Logging | Auto-restore? |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### 7. Outputs / Final Element Actions
| Tag | Action on trip | De-energized state | Feedback tag | Feedback timeout param |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Include any other actions (controller to manual, output clamp, trip of other equipment).

### 8. Reset and Restart
Latch or non-latch, who can reset, reset conditions, and whether reset is blocked while the trip condition persists.

### 9. Alarms and HMI
| Alarm tag | Condition | Priority | Rationalization ref | Operator action |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Include trip first-out indication and bypass status display.

### 10. Configuration Notes
Execution order or scan class, and any behavior that differs from the legacy system, with the reason.

### 11. FAT Test Steps
| Step | Precondition | Action | Expected result (cite Param IDs) | Pass/Fail | Initials |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Cover: normal trip, no trip just above the setpoint, delay timing, bad-quality input, bypass behavior, reset behavior, feedback failure, and alarm presentation.

### 12. Traceability and Open Items
| Legacy item | New item | Differences | Open question / owner |
|---|---|---|---|

---

## Part B: Example, Heater Low Fuel Gas Pressure

> All numeric values and the tags marked *(assumed)* are illustrative placeholders. Confirm against the P&ID, the legacy logic, and the register before use.

### 1. Identification
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID | `H11-IL-005` |
| Title | Heater H-1101 low fuel gas pressure, close main fuel gas valve |
| Unit / Area | Unit 11, Fired Heaters |
| Revision | A (draft for migration review) |
| Legacy source | C&E dwg *(fill in)*, cause row *(fill in)*; logic printout page *(fill in)* |
| New DCS location | Controller *(fill in)*, FB `H11_IL005` |

### 2. Classification and Purpose
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Layer | BPCS |
| Intent | Stop fuel supply on low fuel gas header pressure to avoid flame instability, flameout, and unburned fuel accumulation |
| Consequence if it fails | Burner flameout with continued fuel admission, possible firebox explosion |
| PHA/LOPA credit | **Confirm.** Low fuel gas pressure protection on fired heaters is commonly treated as a BMS/SIS function (see API 556 / IEC 61511 practice). If it is credited anywhere, it belongs in the SRS, not this document. |

### 3. Inputs
| Tag | Description | Range | Bad-quality action | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 | Fuel gas header pressure at heater battery limit | 0–10 barg *(assumed)* | Treat as trip condition (fail-safe) after `H11-P-005-BQ` | AI card *(address)* |
| ZSC-1106 | XV-1106 closed limit switch *(assumed)* | DI | Alarm only | DI card *(address)* |

### 4. Trip Logic
**Statement:** If PT-1105 is below the low-low setpoint continuously for the trip delay, and the interlock is not bypassed, close XV-1106 and latch the trip.

**Expression:**
```
TRIP = ( PT-1105.PV < [H11-P-005-SP] FOR [H11-P-005-TD] s
         OR PT-1105.Quality = BAD FOR [H11-P-005-BQ] s )
       AND NOT BYPASS_ACTIVE
```
Voting: 1oo1.

### 5. Parameters (from register; do not edit here)
| Param ID | Meaning | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| H11-P-005-SP | Trip setpoint (falling) | 1.5 | barg |
| H11-P-005-RS | Reset deadband (trip clears above SP + RS) | 0.2 | barg |
| H11-P-005-TD | Trip on-delay | 2 | s |
| H11-P-005-BQ | Bad-quality persistence before trip | 3 | s |
| H11-P-005-AL | Pre-trip alarm (PAL-1105), falling | 2.0 | barg |
| H11-P-005-FB | Valve closed feedback timeout | 10 | s |

Register: `Interlock_Parameters.xlsx`, sheet *H11*.

### 6. Permissives, Bypasses, Overrides
| Item | Tag | Condition | Authority / Logging | Auto-restore |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Startup bypass | `H11-BYP-005` | **Open item:** the legacy design may bypass during light-off. Confirm whether one exists and its basis. If one is retained, it needs a time limit, an engineer-level key, and an event log. | Supervisor key + log | Yes, after time limit *(param to be added)* |

### 7. Outputs / Final Element Actions
| Tag | Action | De-energized state | Feedback | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| XV-1106 | Command closed (de-energize solenoid) | Closed (fail-closed) | ZSC-1106 | H11-P-005-FB |
| FIC-1107 *(assumed)* | Set to manual, output 0% | n/a | n/a | n/a |

### 8. Reset and Restart
- Latched trip.
- Reset by operator from the faceplate, only when PT-1105 > H11-P-005-SP + H11-P-005-RS and quality is good.
- Reset does not reopen XV-1106. Reopening is a separate operator command under the heater start-up procedure.

### 9. Alarms and HMI
| Alarm | Condition | Priority | Operator action |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAL-1105 | PV < H11-P-005-AL | High *(per rationalization)* | Check fuel gas supply and pressure control |
| H11-IL-005-TRIP | Trip latched | Critical | Verify XV-1106 closed, identify the cause before reset |
| H11-IL-005-FBFAIL | ZSC-1106 not closed within H11-P-005-FB after trip | Critical | Field check, isolate manually |
| H11-IL-005-BYP | Bypass active | High | Confirm bypass is authorized |

The first-out indication appears on the heater overview.

### 10. Configuration Notes
- Compare the legacy delay behavior (on-delay versus filtered PV) and document any difference.
- Execution at the fastest scan class available for this controller.
- The trip block reads parameters from the register-generated tag list. No literals are in the logic.

### 11. FAT Test Steps
| # | Precondition | Action | Expected result | P/F |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PT-1105 simulated at 4.0 barg, XV-1106 open, no bypass | Ramp PV down below H11-P-005-SP and hold longer than H11-P-005-TD | PAL-1105 alarms at H11-P-005-AL. After the delay, XV-1106 commands closed, trip latched, FIC-1107 to manual at 0%, trip alarm shown | |
| 2 | As above | Drop PV below SP for less than H11-P-005-TD, then restore | No trip | |
| 3 | As above | Hold PV just above H11-P-005-SP | No trip, pre-trip alarm active | |
| 4 | Trip latched | Raise PV above SP but below SP + RS, attempt reset | Reset rejected | |
| 5 | Trip latched | Raise PV above SP + RS, reset | Trip clears, XV-1106 stays closed until commanded | |
| 6 | Normal | Force PT-1105 to bad quality for longer than H11-P-005-BQ | Trip as in step 1 | |
| 7 | Normal | Force bad quality for less than H11-P-005-BQ, then restore | No trip | |
| 8 | Trip active | Hold ZSC-1106 not-closed beyond H11-P-005-FB | FBFAIL alarm | |
| 9 | Bypass enabled (if retained) | Repeat step 1 | No trip, bypass alarm active, event logged | |

### 12. Traceability and Open Items
| Legacy | New | Differences | Open question / owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legacy PSL-1105 setpoint *(value)* | H11-P-005-SP | Confirm the value was verified against the last calibration and relief or burner data | Process engineer |
| Legacy bypass (if any) | `H11-BYP-005` | See section 6 | Operations + safety |
| Classification | n/a | BPCS vs. BMS/SIS | Functional safety lead |

---

**Suggestions for rollout across 40 units:** generate the interlock sheets, the configuration tag list, and the FAT parameter columns from the Parameter Register wherever possible. Then a setpoint change in the register propagates everywhere and nobody edits a value by hand. Also run a classification check on each legacy interlock first, so anything that quietly has IPL credit gets moved to the SRS rather than migrated as BPCS.
